# ui::WindowStyle

Header: `winui/ui/WindowStyle.hpp`.

The frame a window is drawn with: caption buttons, sizing border, frame kind, z-order and title-bar extension.

Seed it through [`ui::WindowOptions::style`](window-options.md). To change it live, edit a copy of [Window::style()](window.md#style) and hand it to [Window::set_style()](window.md#set_style), which applies it to the running window. The defaults give a plain resizable window with a caption. [Fill](../layout/fill.md#uifill) it with designated initializers.

Example: 
```cpp
// A fixed-size tool palette that stays on top and has no maximize button.
ui::Window palette{{.title = "Tools",
                    .style = {.resizable = false, .maximize_button = false, .always_on_top = true}}};

// Content under the caption of the main window, with a TitleBar in the 48 DIP row it leaves.
ui::WindowStyle style = window.style();
style.extend_content_into_title_bar = true;
style.title_bar_height              = 48;
window.set_style(style);
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resizable` | `bool` | `true` | A sizing border, and with it drag-to-snap. On `Frame::None` it has no effect: a popup has no border to size by. |
| `minimize_button` | `bool` | `true` | The caption's minimize button (and Win+Down's fallback target). |
| `maximize_button` | `bool` | `true` | The caption's maximize button, maximizing by double-clicking the caption, and Win+Up. Independent of `resizable`. It only limits the user. [Window::request_state()](window.md#request_state) still maximizes a window that has no maximize button. |
| `always_on_top` | `bool` | `false` | Stays above every non-topmost window. Off by default. |
| `frame` | `Frame` | `Frame::Standard` | How much of the frame the OS draws; see [`Frame`](namespace-ui.md#frame). |
| `tool_window` | `bool` | `false` | A short caption, no taskbar button and no entry in Alt+Tab, for a palette or a tool strip that belongs to another window. |
| `closable` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the close button and Alt+F4 are enabled. Off also grays out the system menu's Close item. An app that must stay open also has to refuse to quit when it is asked another way. |
| `animations` | `bool` | `true` | The OS's open/close/minimize/maximize animations. Off suits a kiosk or a remote session. |
| `caption_title` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the caption draws the window title. Only meaningful on `Frame::Standard`; the caption buttons stay either way. |
| `caption_icon` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the caption draws the window icon. Only meaningful on `Frame::Standard`. Without the icon, clicking where it was no longer opens the system menu (Alt+Space and a caption right-click still do). |
| `extend_content_into_title_bar` | `bool` | `false` | Let the client area extend over the caption. The OS keeps drawing the caption buttons and the caption background, and the app lays out its own title row, usually a [TitleBar](../controls/title-bar.md#uititlebar), underneath them. [Window::caption_insets()](window.md#caption_insets) reports the space the buttons take. Only meaningful on `Frame::Standard`. Ignored while fullscreen. |
| `title_bar_height` | `float` | `0.0f` | How tall the extended caption row is at least, in DIPs, when `extend_content_into_title_bar` is on. The row is never shorter than the OS's own caption, so 0 leaves it at that height. A taller row ([TitleBar](../controls/title-bar.md#uititlebar)'s 48 DIP expanded height) extends the caption background further; the buttons stay at the top. |
| `caption_buttons` | `bool` | `true` | The caption's minimize, maximize and close buttons. Off takes all three away, and the system menu with them. Meaningful on `Frame::Standard`, and on `Frame::Borderless` under a system backdrop, where the system would otherwise draw the buttons over the content (a tray flyout turns it off for that). `Frame::None` has no caption at all. [Window::close()](window.md#close) still closes. With content extended into the title bar, off means no buttons and no caption band beyond `title_bar_height`, so 0 leaves no band at all. |
| `round_popup_corners` | `bool` | `false` | On `Frame::None`, gives the popup rounded corners and a 1px rim like a top-level window has, where a bare popup is square. The system's own flyouts (Start, Quick Settings, the calendar) look this way, with no shadow. Applies only while the theme's [`ChromeHints::corner_preference`](../themes/chrome-hints.md) is `Default`, so an era that asks for square corners keeps them. No effect on any other frame, which the system already rounds. |
